verdict.line: You lose if you stand still while Ornn's E (Searing Charge) collides with a wall and chains into his R knockup; you win if you force short Q (Ntofo Strikes) trades and out-scale him after Iceborn Gauntlet comes online.

brief.thesis: Ornn's only real CC threat comes from E (Searing Charge) hitting terrain for a shockwave knockup, and his Q (Volcanic Rupture) outranges your Q (Ntofo Strikes) by 350 units, so he wants to poke and wall-combo you. You win by closing that gap with Q stacks, since two stacks fire a shockwave that pulls him in and erases his range advantage. Lane and solo-kill edge both sit with K'Sante here, matching the 49.2% head-to-head over 956 games — this is close, not lopsided.

theirWindow.when: Ornn E lines up with a wall
theirWindow.what: If his Searing Charge collides with terrain it creates a knockup shockwave around him — back off the moment you see him charge at a wall, because the follow-up stun opens you to a Volcanic Rupture or early R.

yourWindow.when: His Q and E are both down
yourWindow.what: Close to 450 range and land Q twice; the second hit's shockwave pulls him in so he can't kite back to his longer Q range, and your W (Path Maker) charge-up reduces the damage you take while you commit.

powerCurve.note: both ults up, his first R scariest

start.why: Flat magic resist blunts Ornn's magic-damage poke from Q and W long before he has a magic pen item, and it's the standard start at 89.9% pick.

boots.why: Tenacity shortens the knockup from his E wall-collision and the stun window if he lands R, and the magic resist stacks with your early build against his all-magic kit.

core.why: Gives your Q stacking a damage and slow boost so you can actually close the range gap before he resets to max Q distance.
Omnivamp off your Q stacks and autos keeps you healthy through his sustained Bellows Breath trades.
Stacking resistances let you tank the Brittle-boosted burst from his Q pillar and R elemental in extended fights.

situational.when: he's building AP or his magic burst is one-shotting you through shields
you need more armor and slow resistance to survive his E/R knockup chains
the fight is dragging and you need more sustain off your Q and R healing

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the short Q trades you're forced into at 450 range, healing you back through his longer-range Q poke between stacks.

summoners.why: Teleport is the standard pick at 84.3% and lets you reset after shoving with Q stacks; Flash covers the gap when you need to dodge his R elemental redirect.

playing.title: Force short Q trades
playing.detail: Stay inside 450 range and land two Q (Ntofo Strikes) hits; the second stack fires a shockwave that pulls him in, denying the longer-range poke he wants.

playing.title: Watch E for wall collision
playing.detail: Searing Charge only knocks up if it hits terrain — if he's charging in open space, it's just a damage line with no stun, so stand your ground and punish.

playing.title: Use W to blunt his engage
playing.detail: Path Maker's charge-up takes reduced damage before the dash lands, so hold it to eat his E or Q damage and knock him back with the stun on the way out.

playing.title: Reposition early against R
playing.detail: Call of the Forge God's elemental speeds up as it travels, so move off its line the moment it's summoned rather than waiting to see where it's aimed.

playing.title: Chain damage onto Brittle
playing.detail: Bellows Breath's final gout and the Q pillar both apply Brittle; land your Q and W combo while he's Brittle for the extra damage taken.

playing.title: Respect his first R timer
playing.detail: His first Call of the Forge God sits on a 140s cooldown before dropping to 100s, so play safer the first time you see it summoned and more aggressively after.

playing.title: All-in after Iceborn comes online
playing.detail: Once you have Iceborn Gauntlet your Q stacking damage and R's healing win extended fights; look for All Out when his HP is low to secure the kill with the forced dash.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, boots, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers are measured from live games on the current patch; the lane timing, ability reads, and trade patterns are our own tactical analysis.
